# Independent audit: full stochastic cubic and arbitrary triangle transfer

Sources read completely and independently:

* `candidate 2a708bf626836967`;
* `candidate 6b3596acb8604c8b`.


ordinary planar triangle theorem and a standalone matrix theorem; it
does not prove the corresponding assertion for arbitrary convex bodies
or any global mixed-integer theorem.

## 1. Compact spectral maximization and its positive weights

The stochastic polytope is compact. Each row functional is the square
root of a nonnegative maximum of finitely many quadratics, so all edge
weights and the largest eigenvalue are continuous. A spectral maximizer
therefore exists. A value greater than one forces at least two positive
edges: a matrix with at most one has largest eigenvalue at most its sole
edge weight, which is at most one. Two positive edges connect all three
vertices. The Rayleigh-quotient absolute-value argument supplies a
nonnegative maximizing eigenvector, and its eigenvector equations force
strict positivity by graph connectedness. Thus every fixed Rayleigh
weight2w_iw_j used in the local argument is strictly positive, even when
one row functional is zero.

Holding this unit vector fixed gives a weighted sum bounded above by
the largest eigenvalue at every stochastic matrix and equal at the
maximizer. Consequently the spectral maximizer really is a global
weighted-sum maximizer. There is no interchange of an optimization
with a pointwise upper approximation in the wrong direction.

## 2. The local two-full-row perturbation

If two rows are fully positive, every sufficiently small signed transfer
v between them preserves all column sums and all nonnegativity
constraints. The unchanged third row need not be smooth or positive.

At a tied maximum, each active square-root branch is smooth locally
because its quadratic value is positive. Replacing the two varied
row maxima by selected active branches produces a smooth function
bounded ABOVE by the original objective and equal at the alleged local
maximum; it therefore also has a local maximum. The first variations
force the two weighted gradients to agree. Using either of two tied
branches in one row would make their gradients equal, contradicting
the exact difference(x_l/phi)(e_j-e_k), which is nonzero for a full row.
This correctly rules out tied maxima before invoking a Hessian.

For unique maxima, every coordinate of the common weighted gradient
lambda is strictly positive. The two proposed transfer vectors satisfy
lambda dot v=0. If the maximizing columns agree, their common active
quadratic has value lambda_k lambda_l>0 on v. If the columns differ,
both active quadratics have value one. For a quadratic Q with zero
first directional derivative, the second derivative of sqrt(Q) is
Q(v)/sqrt(Q), with no omitted factor of two. Both weighted second
derivatives are positive. The ordering of each unique maximum remains
unchanged locally, so this is an actual positive second variation of
the objective. It contradicts local maximality.

## 3. All boundary cases

Two rows with zeros can always be put in one of the two stated forms.
For zeros in one column, the third-row functional is c+r-cr<=1 and
the column-sum identity is exactly sum F_i=1-(aq+bp); the AM--GM
comparison retains its direction when any factor is zero.

For different zero columns, the three printed differences between Z
and the possible third-row quadratics are exact nonnegative polynomial
identities. In particular F_3<=Z<=1. Both diagonal entries of the
two-by-two matrix N are nonnegative, and its determinant is
(1-F_3)(Z-F_3). These conditions imply PSD even if a diagonal or the
determinant vanishes. Applying it to(sqrt(b),sqrt(e)) gives exactly
the cubic. The L=0 case is separately handled before division.

The equivalence of the cubic with I-B positive semidefinite uses all
principal minors, which are explicitly nonnegative. It is valid with
zero edges or equality. Thus the spectral contradiction closes the
full stochastic domain, not merely its relative interior.

## 4. One-row minimization and arbitrary incidence

The one-row infimum includes h beyond the support, repeated entries,
constant rows, and the zero row. The critical value h*=x+y-xy/z lies
between y and z because h*-y=x(1-y/z)>=0 and
z-h*=(z-x)(z-y)/z>=0. The (0,0,z) infimum is approached at zero,
as explicitly stated, and is not falsely claimed to be attained at a
positive threshold. The derivative agrees across a middle-vertex
level; the transfer only uses a proper cut, so extreme support atoms
of a constant row cannot enter its stationary argument.

For the actual triangle transfer, the divergence cut-face flux is
+t_ij sigma_i. Together with the opposite-edge flux2k R_ij this
gives R_ij=Q_i-t_ij S_i/2 with the printed sign. The cut line passes
through an interior point; it can contain a vertex, but cannot coincide
with a boundary edge. Vertices carry no area or edge length, and the
coarea section length is continuous at an interior vertex level.

Balanced normals give column sums exactly one after division by
S_i M. The distribution identity and derivative are
G_i(a_i)=Q_i and G_i'(a_i)=2M S_i, hence a_i G_i'=2Q_i.
The supporting tangent to the concave square root of this CDF has
zero intercept. Its constant extension beyond the top support is
concave too, so the tangent comparison is valid on the entire domain
used by the row infimum. Thus phi(X_i)=a_i/sqrt(Q_i) for every actual
incidence pattern, including vertex cuts and two-vertex captured caps.

Finally f_i=2phi(X_i) converts the stochastic cubic into
sum f_i^2+f_1f_2f_3<=4 with the exact factors4 and8. The raw section
normalization is sigma_i=length/||u_i||, S_i=sigma_i/k, and
M=sum q_i/sigma_i=sum Q_i/S_i; no normalization is lost. The derived
individual row inequality follows by testing I-B on(1,1,t) and
minimizing over t, yielding(phi_j+phi_l)^2<=2(1-phi_i).

## 5. Independent verification

The source verifier was rerun:36,169 exact checks PASS, including
364 two-vertex and135 vertex-boundary cuts. The independent companion
`supporting computation verify_full_stochastic_cubic_audit_two_sided.py` checks the symbolic
boundary identities, the perturbation quadratics and second derivative,
an independently enumerated stochastic grid, and exact clipping/coarea
normalizations on actual triangles. These checks supplement the proof
audit; they are not substituted for the compactness or perturbation
arguments above.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
